eps.d: John Ho is a Detective Sergeant in London's East End, he's also Chinese. He has to deal with a released prisoner, a smashed window and a terrified wife.
The murder of a Chinese club owner sets John Ho in the middle of a gangland struggle for power - and into the bad books of Chief Inspector Berwick.
Mr. Hong holds the key to a big prize which the Fulham gang are desperate to win. John Ho observes them all - and witnesses the evil result of ambition and greed.
When a villain puts dishonesty behind him, he doesn't want to be reminded of his past by the tax man - or by the tenacious John Ho.
John Ho becomes involved in a complex Chinese puzzle - and goes into hospital to take care of a patient.
John Ho plays for high stakes when he gambles his own life to accomplish his personal mission.
On the first day of the Old Bailey trial, John Ho gets an unwelcome call from his boss Berwick. As well as two OAP's, a 12-bore shotgun and a fleet of three-wheelers.
John Ho has viral pneumonia. Dr Li prescribes 'ten days horizontal', but a visit from informer, Jack Bross, rouses John from his sickbed.
Jack Longman's good with figures but a stolen Mercedes and a ledger, set John Ho on course for another result. Not the one he had in mind.
A mother's cry for help sends John in search of a missing boy. With tapshoes and a cassette player, Tommy is no ordinary boy.
When a Glaswegian gunfighter rides into Limehouse there's blood on the streets. But Doc Halliday's fantasies explode in other people's faces.
Jack Balfe is an East End fence and when he wants distinguished Tenor Robert Tear to sing at his daughter's 21st. No one, least of all John Ho, is going to stop him.
Routine searches and an irritable Berwick don't appeal to John Ho. When a pile of bones is found in a derelict house, Ho sees a chance to escape both.
A fatal shooting occurs and the only witness is an old lady and her budgies! Then other parties show interest..
